Smoothing
Temporal averaging

Fast responds quickest, Slow is a steadier average, and Inf keeps a running average until Reset averaging. Custom means a custom curve is active; switch Settings mode to Advanced to edit its times. The full 1–10 scale is also in Advanced.

1 and 3 are FIFO averages of 2 and 8 FFT analysis frames. 2 holds a 133 ms window — four frames at the normal 30 Hz cadence, time-weighted at lower frame rates — and the oldest frame drops out as a new one arrives. 4–10 are frequency-weighted: lows average longer than highs. 6 is the recommended general starting point; Inf keeps a running average until Reset averaging. Custom opens the time-constant controls below.

10–60,000 ms. Low/high blends across frequency like presets 4–10; whole band applies one time constant to every band.

IN1

Mirrors whatever the OS exposes: built-in mic, headset, or a USB audio interface. 1+2 measures both channels of a stereo interface at once — a measurement mic on input 1 against a console feed on input 2 — and overlays them on the RTA. Each plot can follow either input, and each capture channel keeps its own trim. A mono input shows the same signal on both.

No calibration file for this channel.

Choose a text file with a Frequency (Hz) column and one response column explicitly labeled in dB (such as Response (dB), Mic Response dB, or Sensitivity dB). Extra columns are accepted only when the header identifies the response column. The app subtracts the listed response and interpolates by log frequency. Channel 1 is left and channel 2 is right on the one selected input device, not separate devices. In Mix mode a stereo input is summed, so no channel calibration is applied; use Left, Right, or 1+2. Apply calibration bypasses correction for quick A/B; the CAL badge shows which analyzed channels are corrected. Saved curves are labeled by device and channel and can be assigned to the selected input. Storage is matched to the active stream's browser-reported input ID and left/right channel; if the active input reports no ID, no calibration is applied. Browsers may reset or reuse IDs, so this cannot guarantee physical-microphone identity. Verify the selected input and calibration after browser/device changes; stale calibrations may be removed. This corrects frequency response only; readings remain relative dBFS, not SPL.

EQ file layout

The 31-band file is one gain per ISO third-octave centre (20 Hz – 20 kHz), clamped to ±12 dB and rounded to 0.5 dB — the range a graphic EQ can actually take. With a target curve shown the gains correct towards it; without one they correct towards the 500 Hz – 2 kHz average, so the house curve is left alone.

About

Two-input real-time analyzer: fractional-octave RTA, spectrograph with rewind, 1+2 input overlay, draggable A/B frequency markers with zoom to the selection, captured traces with spatial averaging, and target curves for FOH, monitors, cars and listening rooms. Levels are relative full-scale (dBFS); this build has no SPL metering and no calibrated absolute levels. Independent implementation — not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Rational Acoustics. Overlaid inputs are two independent RTAs: there is no transfer function, no impulse response and no .srf interchange.
